title: Topic Cluster Drift in Second Brain
dataSources: Reading progress (`reading:progress`), highlights (`highlight:capture`), note links (`note:link`), books finished (`book:finished`).
app: Reading and knowledge-management telemetry — Goodreads / StoryGraph libraries, Kindle highlights (Readwise), and note-graph exports (Obsidian, Notion) — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=note:link topic=*
| bin _time span=1mon
| stats dc(note) as notes by _time topic
| eventstats sum(notes) as total by _time
| eval topic_share=round(100*notes/total,1)
| sort 0 _time - topic_share
description: Shows which subjects are dominating your notes month by month and whether your focus is becoming too narrow.
value: A second brain can overfit to the topic you are obsessed with this month; topic-share drift provides a balance check.
implementation: Tag notes with a primary topic and chart monthly share by topic across the note graph.
visualization: Stacked area chart of monthly note share by topic.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces which subjects are taking over your notes and whether the balance of your reading and thinking is shifting too far.
